title: Best Window of K Distinct Values
statement:
You get an array of positive integers nums and a window length k.

Look at every contiguous block of exactly k elements. A block is valid only if all its values are different. Return the largest sum of a valid block, or 0 if no block of length k is valid.

examples.why: [4, 2, 4] repeats 4 and is skipped. The valid blocks sum to 11 ([2, 4, 5]), 10 and 9.
Every block of two repeats 7, so there is no valid block.
[9, 9] has the biggest sum but is not valid. [9, 1] is the best valid block.

hints: Neighbouring blocks share k − 1 elements. Can you update both the sum and the repeat check when the block slides by one?
Keep a count of each value inside the window. The window is valid exactly when the number of distinct values equals k.
Slide: add nums[i], remove nums[i − k], update the sum and the counts (delete a value when its count hits 0). When the map has k keys, compare the sum with the best.

explain.intuition:
Checking each block from scratch costs O(k) per block. But block i and block i + 1 differ by one element entering and one leaving, like a carousel that shows k items and scrolls by one. So keep a running sum and a value-to-count map for the current block and adjust both by one element at each step.

The validity test then becomes free: k elements are all different exactly when the map holds k distinct keys. Remove a key when its count drops to zero, or the size will lie.
steps: Walk i from 0 to n − 1. Add nums[i] to the sum and increment its count.
If i ≥ k, remove nums[i − k]: subtract it from the sum and decrement its count, deleting the key at zero.
If i ≥ k − 1 and the map has exactly k keys, update best = max(best, sum).
Return best, which stays 0 if no block was valid.
pitfalls: Not deleting keys whose count drops to zero. The map size then overcounts distinct values and valid blocks are missed.
Shrinking the window to a shorter length when a repeat appears and scoring that shorter block. Only blocks of length exactly k count.
Checking validity before removing the element that leaves the window.

solutions.title: Check every block
solutions.idea: For each start, build a set of the next k values. If the set reaches size k, the block is valid; compare its sum.

solutions.title: Fixed-size sliding window with counts
solutions.idea: Slide a window of length k, keeping its sum and a count per value. The window is valid when the map has k keys.

followups: Allow at most one repeated value inside a block. What do you track instead of the map size?
Drop the fixed length: find the largest sum of any contiguous block with all values different. How does the window move now?
lcTitle: Maximum Sum of Distinct Subarrays With Length K
